_comment: Chronicle grammar for the Houses of the Maze (plan T1.8). Keys are EventType names, some with a suffix the renderer picks (_LORD_SLAIN, _FORCED, _UNKNOWN). Each has NEUTRAL (rumour), FOR (the acting house's scribe) and AGAINST (its enemy's scribe). Tokens: {A} {B} house names, {a} {b} figure names, {place}, {gash}, {year}, {cb}, {wordsA}, {sigilA}, {ordinal}. #symbol# expands from symbols, voice first. ASCII only, and within the content ceiling of plan D4 (ContentCeilingTest).

NEUTRAL: In the year {year}, {A} raised a banner of {sigilA} and called itself a house.
{A} was founded in the year {year}. Its words were {wordsA}.
The year {year} saw {a} plant {sigilA} in the black soil and name it {A}.
FOR: In the year {year} {a} took up {sigilA} and swore {wordsA} upon the bones of the old. So {A} began, and so it endures.
Before the counting of years was finished, {a} cut the first stone of {A}. #grim_detail#
{A} did not ask leave to exist. In the year {year} {a} simply declared it, and the Maze was obliged to listen.
AGAINST: In the year {year} a nobody called {a} sewed {sigilA} onto a rag and named the rag {A}.
{A} was born in the year {year}, the way a blister is born: from friction, and of no use to anyone.
They say {A} was founded in the year {year}. Founded is a generous word for it.

The year {year}: the Antlered Lord came up through the Obsidian Rift and took the castle that bears his name.
No one agrees on how the Rift opened in the year {year}. Everyone agrees on what came through it.
FOR: In the year {year} the Rift knelt open for its master. Tarmin-Zul stepped through, and the world remembered how to bow.
The Antlered Lord rose in the year {year}. The castle was waiting for him. It had always been waiting.
In the year {year} the door was opened, and the door was ours. {wordsA}.
AGAINST: In the year {year} a beast with a crown of antlers clawed out of the Obsidian Rift and named itself a lord.
Mark the year {year}, when the Rift bled out its worst. The thing called Tarmin-Zul has squatted in its stolen castle ever since.
The year {year}. The Rift opened, and the Antlered Usurper crawled out of it. #grim_detail#

{b} died and {a} inherited everything except the wit to keep it. The year was {year}.
{A} crowned {a} in the year {year}. #weather_omen#

{b} disputed the seat of {A}, and {a} disputed {b}'s right to keep breathing. The year was {year}. #grim_detail#
When {b} reached for the circlet in the year {year}, {a} broke the hand that reached.
AGAINST: In the year {year} {a} stole the seat of {A} out from under {b}, and the scribes were paid to call it law.
{b} had the better claim. {a} had more swords. In the year {year}, swords won, as they do.
The house of {A} tore itself in half in the year {year}, and {a} wore the larger half.

grim_detail: The ditches were full for a month.
The crows were fat that year.
No one sang about it afterward.
Some of the bodies were never named.
The smoke could be seen from three holdfasts.
The bells rang until the ropes broke.
battle_aftermath: The crows ate well for a fortnight.
The survivors were made to dig the pits.
The banners of the dead were burned on the field.
The heads went up on the gate by nightfall.
The river ran slow and dark for a week.
weather_omen: The wells went bitter that year.
A two-headed calf was born the same week. No one took it for a good sign.
The bells cracked in the cold.
That winter the dead did not stay buried.

grim_detail: The choir sang over the dead, and the dead were grateful.
Every wound was counted, as the hymn requires.
The Host does not count its dead. It counts its enemies'.
The antlers were dipped in it.
The bones were catalogued and stored.
The ossuary needed a new wing.
They ate before the fires were lit.
It was not discussed at court.
The tapestries were changed that season.
The chains were counted and found sufficient.
Every captive was tallied and hooked.

talk._comment: Town folk's greetings by role (plan T4.3). Slots: {town}, {allegiance}, {house} (an exile's fallen house), {war} (a war being fought above, or 'the houses'), {predecessor} (who held the seat before, or 'the founders').
SMITH: Bring me iron from the dead and I will make it sing.
Half my iron comes off the fields where {war} bleed each other. I do not ask whose it was.
{predecessor} taught me this forge. I have not shamed it yet.
INNKEEPER: Sit. Drink. Nobody asks names under the ground.
The beds are hard and the walls are thick. That is the whole of the welcome.
Every traveller this season talks of {war}. Drink, and talk of something else.
This house was kept by {predecessor} before me. The ale has not improved.
QUESTGIVER: There is always work for someone who comes back.
You have the look of someone the Maze has not finished with.
While {war} are at each other's throats, {town} can get things done. Sit down.
ELDER: We were farmers once, before the gashes. Now we are moles.
Every year the houses come closer. Every year we dig deeper.
{allegiance} have outlasted worse than {war}. We will outlast them too.
{predecessor} kept {town} before me, and buried more seekers than I have. Mind yourself.
COMMONER: Mind the dark past the lamps.
You came from up there? Gods.
They say {war} are fighting over our heads again. You can hear it in the rock, some nights.
MERCHANT: Coin is coin, down here as anywhere.
Buy, sell, or stand aside. {town} has other custom.
EXILE: I was sworn to {house}. The blood I served is ash, and I am still here. Make of that what you like.
Ask the chronicles what became of {house}. I was there. I would rather not tell it.
The mortals let me sit by their fire. {house} never once did that.
HOSTILE: Get out. {town} remembers what you did.
We have nothing for you. Get out, before the guards are called.
